_about: Hand-checked against Jerrythafast/FDSTools at 5cad6d057fd2f16bd77f9aa2420e920ccfcc7aa6 (untagged in repos.tsv, but this commit is git tag v2.2.1) on 2026-09-29, from README.md, pyproject.toml, fdstools/tools/pipeline.py, fdstools/lib/cli.py, fdstools/lib/library.py and fdstools/data/libraries/ at that commit, the project site named in pyproject.toml (https://fdstools.nl: guide.html, tools.html), api.anaconda.org and PyPI.

command.where: https://fdstools.nl/tools.html#pipeline (the same text is the built-in help, fdstools/tools/pipeline.py:36-41, shown by `fdstools --help pipeline` as README.md:9-12 directs)

input.where: README.md:3-4; https://fdstools.nl/tools.html#pipeline (-s/--in-sample-raw: FastA or FastQ file); https://fdstools.nl/guide.html (1. targeted, amplicon-based MPS of forensic markers)

extra_inputs.what: FDSTools library file (marker definitions, INI) for the kit. It is built into FDSTools as 'ForenSeqA', 'ForenSeqA-UAS', 'ForenSeqB', 'ForenSeqB-UAS', 'ID-OmniSTR' or 'PowerSeq46GY', so STRhub's ForenSeq kit context is enough to pick 'ForenSeqB' (the NIST sample is primer mix B)
extra_inputs.where: https://fdstools.nl/tools.html#pipeline (-l/--in-library); https://fdstools.nl/tools.html#tssv (LIBRARY: custom file or built-in); fdstools/lib/cli.py:62-67; fdstools/lib/library.py:46-49; fdstools/data/libraries/ForenSeqB.ini:1-2

extra_inputs.what: stutter model from Stuttermodel (-m/--in-stuttermodel), trained on homozygous reference samples
background noise profiles from BGEstimate (-p/--in-bgprofiles), built from reference samples

runnable_on_strhub_data.why: The case-sample pipeline requires only the raw sample FASTQ and a library (fdstools/tools/pipeline.py:598-605). STRhub's illumina-str-fastq is a ForenSeq primer-mix-B sample, and FDSTools ships the matching built-in 'ForenSeqB' library. The stutter model and noise profiles are optional (pipeline.py:601-602). No reference FASTA is needed, because flank sequence comes from the strnaming dependency (fdstools/lib/library.py:27,174). The tool writes the INI itself.

notes: The README gives no analysis command, only `fdstools --help [TOOLNAME]` (README.md:7,12) and pip install. Usage lives in the built-in per-tool help, which https://fdstools.nl/tools.html reproduces. The guide's 'Getting started: Basic sample analysis' section is empty (guide.html calls the guide a work in progress). The documented invocation writes a default INI when the file does not exist and runs the analysis when it does (fdstools/tools/pipeline.py:942-962). Values given with -l/--in-library and -s/--in-sample-raw become the INI defaults (pipeline.py:862) and are merged into an existing INI (pipeline.py:822-826). So a faithful run is `fdstools pipeline case.ini -a case-sample -l ForenSeqB -s sample.fastq`, issued twice: the first call writes the INI, the second runs it. case-sample runs TSSV, then BGPredict/BGMerge/BGCorrect only when a stutter model or profiles are given, then Samplestats (threshold-based allele calling), seqconvert and vis (pipeline.py:596-680). Output is <tag>.csv and <tag>.html (pipeline.py:670,676). The step that calls alleles is Samplestats; `fdstools tssv` then `fdstools samplestats` by hand is the unpiped equivalent. Bam2fds (new in 2.2.0, README.md:39-42) reads aligned WGS BAMs with a library, but it is not the documented main flow. repos.tsv and the snapshot's tree.json leave the tag empty, but the pinned commit is tag v2.2.1 (2026-08-11). The site's front page and install text still speak of v2.1 and Python 3.5+, while README.md:17 requires Python 3.9.
